title: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 6 (17 Marks · 25 Min)
subject: biology-12

questions.question: Which respiratory pigment found inside skeletal muscle fibers binds oxygen with higher affinity than hemoglobin, storing oxygen for muscular activity?
questions.explanation: Myoglobin is a monomeric iron-containing heme protein with a hyperbolic oxygen binding curve and significantly higher affinity for O2 than tetrameric hemoglobin, storing oxygen in muscle until extreme tissue hypoxia occurs.

questions.question: In the renal corpuscle, which specialized epithelial cells with interdigitating foot processes (pedicels) wrap around glomerular capillaries to form filtration slits?
questions.explanation: Podocytes are specialized visceral epithelial cells of Bowman's capsule whose pedicels interdigitate to create filtration slits bridged by nephrin slit diaphragms, preventing passage of large serum proteins.

questions.question: What structural feature connects cardiac muscle cells end-to-end, containing desmosomes for mechanical adhesion and gap junctions for electrical syncytium?
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs join cardiomyocytes mechanically (via fascia adherens and desmosomes) and electrically (via low-resistance gap junctions), allowing synchronized wave-like depolarization of the myocardium.

questions.question: The resting membrane potential (-70 mV) of a human neuron is primarily created and maintained by:

options.A: Passive entry of sodium and exit of chloride
options.B: The electrogenic Na+/K+ ATPase pump and high resting K+ leak channel permeability
options.D: Equal distribution of anions inside and outside the cell

questions.explanation: The Na+/K+ pump actively expels 3 Na+ for every 2 K+ brought in, while background potassium leak channels allow outward K+ diffusion, keeping the interior of the resting membrane negative at ~ -70 mV.

questions.question: Which pituitary hormone stimulates thyroid follicular cells to synthesize and secrete thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3)?
questions.explanation: TSH, released from the anterior pituitary under the influence of hypothalamic TRH, binds to GPCR receptors on thyroid follicular cells, stimulating iodine trapping, thyroglobulin iodination, and release of T3 and T4.

questions.question: In honeybee colonies, which communication behavior discovered by Karl von Frisch conveys both direction and distance of a nectar source relative to the sun?
questions.explanation: Karl von Frisch decoded the waggle dance of Apis mellifera: the orientation of the waggle run relative to gravity encodes direction relative to the sun, while the duration of the waggle run indicates distance to the food source.

questions.question: The entry of multiple sperm into a single ovum during fertilization (polyspermy) is permanently blocked by:

options.B: The cortical reaction hardening the zona pellucida into a fertilization membrane

questions.explanation: The slow block to polyspermy involves intracellular calcium release triggering exocytosis of cortical granules, which release proteases that hydrolyze ZP3 receptors and crosslink the zona pellucida (zona reaction).

questions.question: What is the primary function of telomeres at the ends of eukaryotic linear chromosomes?

options.B: Preventing chromosomal degradation, end-to-end fusion, and loss of vital genetic sequences during replication
options.C: Directing spindle fiber attachment during metaphase

questions.explanation: Telomeres consist of repetitive non-coding sequences (TTAGGG in humans) that protect chromosome ends from shortening during incomplete lagging-strand replication and prevent DNA repair systems from misidentifying them as double-strand breaks.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the transcription of protein-coding genes into messenger RNA (mRNA) in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: RNA Polymerase II synthesizes all eukaryotic protein-coding mRNA precursors (pre-mRNA) and most snRNAs, whereas RNA Polymerase I transcribes major rRNAs and RNA Polymerase III synthesizes tRNAs and 5S rRNA.

questions.question: What genetic interaction describes a phenomenon where a single gene influences multiple unrelated phenotypic traits (e.g., Marfan syndrome or Sickle cell anemia)?
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy occurs when a mutation in a single gene has multiple, seemingly disparate phenotypic consequences across multiple organ systems (e.g., sickle hemoglobin causing anemia, splenic infarcts, and stroke).

questions.question: The reduced genetic diversity observed when a small founding cohort establishes a new colony isolated from the parent population is called:
questions.explanation: The founder effect is a form of genetic drift that occurs when a few individuals colonize a new habitat, carrying only a non-random fraction of the parent population's genetic variance.

questions.question: What technique uses short fluorescent single-stranded DNA or RNA probes to locate specific nucleotide sequences directly on intact metaphase chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) utilizes fluorescently labeled complementary DNA/RNA probes to hybridize to target chromosomal regions, allowing direct microscopic visualization of deletions or translocations.

questions.question: A terrestrial biome characterized by permafrost, extremely low temperatures, absence of tall trees, and dominant lichens and mosses is the:
questions.explanation: The Arctic and Alpine Tundra biomes are defined by permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost), short growing seasons, low precipitation, and dwarf vegetation like lichens, sedges, and mosses.

questions.question: In human lung physiology, what is the anatomical dead space volume (air filling conducting airways that does not participate in gas exchange)?
questions.explanation: Anatomical dead space encompasses the conducting zone (nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles) where no gas exchange occurs, typically measuring ~150 mL in an average human.

questions.question: Which condition results from autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex, causing deficiency of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids, hyperpigmentation, and severe hypotension?
questions.explanation: Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) features autoimmune destruction of all adrenal cortical zones, resulting in low cortisol and aldosterone, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, skin hyperpigmentation, and hypotension.

questions.question: During pre-mRNA processing in eukaryotic nuclei, which intervening non-coding sequences are excised by spliceosomes prior to export to the cytoplasm?
questions.explanation: Introns (intervening non-coding sequences) are cleaved from pre-mRNA and degraded by the spliceosome complex (snRNPs), while coding exons are spliced together to form mature mRNA.

questions.question: Which of the following international treaties was signed in 1987 to phase out production and consumption of ozone-depleting chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer (1987) is the landmark international agreement successfully mandating global phase-out of CFCs and halons to recover the stratospheric ozone layer.
